key_insight: Cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsation suppresses turbulence during acceleration, while delayed turbulent shear recovery sustains a low-drag interval before turbulence reorganises.
engineering_relevance: Phase-resolved links between pulsation, turbulence recovery and drag can inform waveform design for pulsatile pipe-flow systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of four waveform-driven pipe-flow cases across two Reynolds-number ranges.
Comparison of waveforms with and without a low-flow plateau.
Phase-resolved turbulence analysis and unsteady friction decomposition.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated cases, streamwise-stress production recovers before redistribution and radial transport, while a low-flow plateau prolongs decay and delays local instability.
watch_item: The findings cover four simulated pipe-flow cases; applicability to broader Reynolds numbers, complex geometries or physiological flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
